findings.title: Stray submodule pointer committed to repository root
findings.body: A file named sentry-repo is added containing a gitlink-style 'Subproject commit' line pointing at the base commit. This is unrelated to error upsampling and will break or confuse checkouts/tooling that does not expect a submodule at that path.

findings.title: Python hash() used in cache keys is not stable across processes
findings.body: The cache key uses hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash for ints is deterministic, but hash() of tuples is process-dependent only for str/bytes; here it is fine by accident, yet the key is also not tied to the allowlist content: the cached eligibility is keyed only by org and projects, so after the allowlist option changes the cached True/False persists for 60s across all workers, and invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called from the option-change path. Using hash() also gives collisions that can return a wrong cached eligibility for a different project set.

findings.title: Cached eligibility bypasses the fresh allowlist check and is inconsistent with the docstring
findings.body: The docstring and _are_all_projects_error_upsampled note claim the allowlist is read fresh each time, yet is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects serves a 60-second cached value. The two statements contradict each other, and the cache hash collision risk means one project set can receive another's eligibility, causing upsampled counts to be applied to projects not in the allowlist, silently inflating counts.

findings.title: Allowlist membership check is O(n) per project against a list option
findings.body: project_id in allowlist scans the option list for every project; with a large allowlist and many projects this is quadratic in work per request. Convert to a set once. Minor on its own but in the hot path of every events-stats request.

findings.title: upsampled_count aggregate ignores sample_weight semantics and returns sum over all rows
findings.body: The new upsampled_count function is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no check that sample_weight is non-null. Events without sample_weight (or from non-allowlisted projects in mixed queries) contribute null/zero, silently undercounting, and the transform's comment that the schema guarantees the column exists is unverified. Also default_result_type 'number' is inconsistent with the 'integer' type used by count().

findings.title: Upsampling is applied to the wrong columns: transform occurs only when top_events or rpc, and reassigns final_columns after use
findings.body: The transform is computed inside each branch using query_columns, but final_columns is initialized once and the rpc/top-events branches each recompute from query_columns, so behavior is correct only by accident. More importantly, count() is rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count' even though the response consumers and the zerofill/other-column logic expect the count alias semantics; the alias is embedded in a column string rather than passed through the normal parser, which may break equations and orderby referencing count().

findings.title: Misleading comments claim caching and late optimization that do not exist
findings.body: The comments say the cached result ensures consistent behavior and that the separation enables caching and query optimization; no such caching of the upsampling decision across query execution exists, the decision is recomputed per call. These comments will mislead maintainers.

findings.title: Unrelated error message change alters public API response text
findings.body: The topEvents validation message is changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is unrelated to upsampling and changes an API response string that clients or tests may match on.

findings.title: Blanket except-pass hides invalid sample rate data
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling swallows all exceptions silently, including from a malformed contexts structure, and sets sample_rate on normalized event data in the shared test factory for all events. Changing store_event behavior for every test that includes an error_sampling context makes the test helper a hidden side effect.

findings.title: Tests create organization and projects with unused fixtures and do not test cache or is_errors_query path
findings.body: The main entry point is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects and its caching behavior, plus invalidate_upsampling_cache, are not tested at all. The snuba_params fixture is built but unused by any test.

findings.title: Endpoint tests mock the options module but the cache is not cleared between tests and assertions are unverified
findings.body: The new endpoint tests rely on the 60-second cache inside is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects without clearing it, so results depend on test ordering across the allowlist cases. Also setUp overwrites self.user after creating projects and assigns self.authed_user before reassigning, and the count assertions (10 per bucket) are not derived from the stored events, which contain only one event per bucket, so the expected value of 10 is suspicious and likely wrong.

findings.title: Transaction test asserts count of 1 for a query that filters on transactions in an errors-focused path
findings.body: test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events stores a transaction and expects count 1 in bucket one and 0 in bucket two, but the earlier error events fall in those same buckets with the errors query path; the expectation does not clearly isolate the transaction behavior and may pass for the wrong reason.
